correctness.rationale: Every nonzero real degree-three harmonic splits into the four O(2) azimuthal sectors. Associated Legendre squares integrate exactly to four rational polynomials; all six exact pair differences factor as products with determined signs, with the one quartic equal to 15(t^2-2/5)^2+13/5. Hence the three strict regimes and only two interior crossing values are proved, and the spectral theorem yields sharp energy bounds, eigenspaces and restriction condition number. The embedded Python checker independently constructs coefficients and factors using rational arithmetic and passes all tests.

originality.rationale: The precise fixed-degree cubic pair-cap phase diagram and five-dimensional resonance were not found in the inspected primary general Slepian literature, the public research database, or accessible own-claim ledger. General matrices and parity decomposition are acknowledged as known, and their calculational implications compared; the new classification depends on separate six-polynomial sign analysis. One old relevant article is inaccessible, leaving explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: Gilbert–Slepian (1977) full text unavailable; its two-interval polynomial analysis may include related low-degree identities, though no supplied evidence resolves or implies the four-sector spherical ordering.
An older unindexed exact associated-Legendre comparison might state the same two roots and phase diagram.
General spherical Slepian matrix formulas make the present low-degree specialization computable; the novelty claim rests on the complete sharp branch classification, not the cap-integral formalism.
